findings.message: For convection, a dome's outside loses heat as a flat roof facing up, over its whole area: no correlation for a curved shell is sourced, so its loss is less certain.
findings.reference: thermal-properties.md §5 (Incropera, Çengel, Lloyd & Moran)

findings.message: Morgan Thermal Ceramics JM 26 insulating firebrick runs up to 2345 °F (data to 2012 °F); past its data sheet's points the conductivity is carried on along the nearest pair of points above the data, and held at the first point's value below it (no lower: more heat loss, the safe side).
findings.reference: electric-and-thermal.md §4.1, Morgan JM IFB series data sheet, 01 January 2025, BR.05

findings.message: Morgan Thermal Ceramics K-23 insulating firebrick runs down to 230.8 °F (data from 500 °F); past its data sheet's points the conductivity is carried on along the nearest pair of points above the data, and held at the first point's value below it (no lower: more heat loss, the safe side).
findings.reference: electric-and-thermal.md §4.1, Morgan K IFB series [S31]

findings.message: Morgan Kaowool ceramic fibre blanket, 8 pcf runs down to 173 °F (data from 500 °F); past its data sheet's points the conductivity is carried on along the nearest pair of points above the data, and held at the first point's value below it (no lower: more heat loss, the safe side).
findings.reference: electric-and-thermal.md §4.3, Foundry Service Kaowool blanket page [S39]

findings.message: HarbisonWalker Kast-O-Lite 30 LI Plus insulating castable runs up to 2345 °F (data to 2000 °F); past its data sheet's points the conductivity is carried on along the nearest pair of points above the data, and held at the first point's value below it (no lower: more heat loss, the safe side).
findings.reference: combustion-and-masonry.md §6.1, HWI Kast-O-Lite 30 LI Plus data 10/19 [S50]; verified on the sheet, door-headers.md [H17]; castables.md §14

findings.message: Some material data comes from extracts of the makers' data sheets and should be checked against the sheets themselves: Morgan Thermal Ceramics K-23 insulating firebrick
Heat loss is the steady loss with the kiln held at top temperature. It does not include the heat stored in the walls and ware during the firing.

The tool chose the fewest burners that carry the input (2 × Ransome B4). Olsen's builds use several: a 20 ft³ cross-draft on four, a 36 ft³ cross-draft on six and an IFB updraft that size on at least ten (p.226–228). No source gives a rule for the count; set burners.count to spread the heat over more.
findings.reference: Olsen, The Kiln Book, 4th ed., p.226–228; kiln-reference.md

findings.message: Cylinders joined in parallel are assumed to add their capacities. That is a reasonable inference at the same temperature and fill, but no source states it. Never warm a cylinder with a flame or heater.
findings.reference: combustion-and-masonry.md §2.6 [S23, S24]

findings.message: Above the kiln a ventilation hood and stack carry the flue gases out of the building, above where people are (Olsen p.151).
findings.reference: Olsen, The Kiln Book, 4th ed., p.151: with burners, the chimney as tall as the kiln or level with its top framework, then a ventilation hood and stack

findings.message: Gas piping, regulators, safety valves and the installation must be done or checked by a licensed gas fitter to your local code (NFPA 54 and 58 in the US).
The front wall is the door: bricked up, dry, for each firing. Lay the inner and outer courses together, staggered, with a header course two-thirds of the way up.
findings.reference: kiln-hardware.md §6.1 [S4]

findings.message: Side-mounted burners need a bag wall so the flames don't hit the ware: hard brick, first course solid in front of the burners.
findings.reference: kiln-hardware.md §1.3 [S4]

findings.message: Damper: a kiln shelf in a slot 12 in wide and one course high, about a foot above the top of the flue. Brace the chimney with angle at its corners and tie it to the kiln frame.
findings.reference: kiln-hardware.md §3.2–3.3 [S4]

findings.message: 4 spy holes, 2 in round, up the door, a few inches off centre so they miss the shelf posts. Cone packs in the top and bottom, draw rings in the middle.
findings.reference: kiln-hardware.md §2 [S4] [S13]

findings.message: Arch bricks: Left wall, layer 1 from the inside, above the springline: about 5 bricks by volume, cut to the curve; Right wall, layer 1 from the inside, above the springline: about 5 bricks by volume, cut to the curve; Back wall, layer 1 from the inside, above the springline: about 2 bricks by volume, cut to the curve; Door, layer 1 from the inside, above the springline: about 2 bricks by volume, cut to the curve; Left wall, layer 2 from the inside, above the springline: about 1 brick by volume, cut to the curve; Right wall, layer 2 from the inside, above the springline: about 1 brick by volume, cut to the curve; Back wall, layer 2 from the inside, above the springline: about 1 brick by volume, cut to the curve; Door, layer 2 from the inside, above the springline: about 1 brick by volume, cut to the curve.
findings.reference: Arch and wedge shapes, 9-inch series; electric-and-thermal.md §5 [S54]

findings.message: Castable: cure 16–24 h above 60 °F kept damp, never let it freeze, and dry it out slowly before the first firing (for Mizzou: 75 °F/h with a ½ h hold per inch at 250, 500 and 1000 °F). Follow the maker's sheet for your castable.
findings.reference: combustion-and-masonry.md §6.2 [S54, S56]

findings.message: Brick counts assume dry joints at the nominal 9 × 4½ × 2½ in size, a ⅛ in saw cut, and 5 % extra for breakage. Each cut piece already takes its own brick in the count. The size is sourced; the saw cut is an assumption no source gives, so adjust it to your saw. The allowance is the masonry estimators' "at least 5 percent" (BIA): set allowances.brick in the design from your own experience. At the corners the side walls run through and the back and door fit between them, layer by layer.
findings.reference: 9 × 4½ × 2½ in straight; electric-and-thermal.md §5 [S54]; kerf assumed; brick-waste.md §1, BIA Technical Note 10 (2009), p.11 [W1]

findings.message: Brick counts assume dry joints at the nominal 9 × 4½ × 2½ in size, a ⅛ in saw cut, and 5 % extra for breakage. Each cut piece already takes its own brick in the count. The allowance is the masonry estimators' "at least 5 percent" (BIA): set allowances.brick in the design from your own experience. At the corners the side walls run through and the back and door fit between them, layer by layer.
